clue.text: Unfinished line in literary collection is proper study for us

indicators.note: in says the shortened line sits inside the literary collection

parts.note: an anthology is a collection of literary pieces

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for line loses its final letter

parts.note: a line is a rope, in the nautical sense

explanation.surface: A scholar recommends a part-finished line of verse in an anthology as proper reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the last letter of the line word before it goes 'in' the collection. The definition echoes Pope's line 'The proper study of mankind is man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the science of humankind, so it is the fitting subject for people to study, as Pope said.

clue.text: A policy-maker, like a certain monarch

parts.note: as means like, in comparison
sure means certain
R is short for rex or regina, a king or queen

explanation.surface: Someone who drafts policy is compared to a monarch of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policy' looks political but is an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance company or underwriter issues policies, so it is a policy provider.

clue.text: Capital is subject to VAT

indicators.note: subject to means placed under, so in this down entry one piece sits below the other

parts.note: a tun is a large vat or cask
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money is taxed with Value Added Tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT looks like the British sales tax but is a plain vat. Tunis is the capital of Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia.

clue.text: Aussie flyer gets sack over prison sentence

indicators.note: over means placed above, the down entry putting one piece before the next

parts.note: to sack a place is to ransack or rifle it
bird is British slang for time in jail, from 'birdlime', rhyming slang for time

explanation.surface: An Australian pilot is fired after serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' wants to mean dismiss; it means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The riflebird is a bird of paradise native to Australia, so an Australian creature that flies.

clue.text: Try to support flower with a stick

indicators.note: to support means to stand underneath, putting one piece below in this down entry

parts.note: the Po is a river, a thing that flows, in crossword slang a flower
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A gardener tries to prop up a bloom with a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword joke for a river (something that flows): the Po in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogo is a spring-loaded jumping toy used to bounce around on.

clue.text: One leering, perhaps, at underwear

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man ogles a display of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I and LEERING together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing and nightwear.

clue.text: Was punished, it's understood

explanation.surface: Someone was disciplined and everybody knows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get it means to be told off or punished, and also to grasp something, as in 'I see, understood'.

clue.text: Monster horse covered with insects

indicators.note: covered with puts one letter inside the first of the insects

parts.note: a bee is an insect
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A dreadful beast of a horse is swarming with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'insects' supplies two different insects; 'covered with' puts the horse inside the first. Horse is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: The behemoth is a huge beast from the Book of Job, so any enormous creature.

clue.text: Mushroom feast

explanation.surface: A banquet of fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow and extend rapidly, and a spread is also a lavish meal laid out.

clue.text: Colt, perhaps, gets a jocular greeting

explanation.surface: A young horse is welcomed with a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt is a famous make of revolver, so a Colt is a gun's offspring in jest; the phrase is also a hearty old exclamation of greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colt revolver is playfully a firearm's child, and the phrase is also a friendly, teasing way of hailing someone.

clue.text: The city without an idiot

indicators.note: without means the word for an is removed from the city

parts.note: Antwerp is a Belgian port city
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes the city as lacking a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes AN from the start of ANTWERP.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, foolish person, a mild British insult.

clue.text: Early prints of Moses' birthplace

explanation.surface: First photographs of the place where Moses was born.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue begins with stray OCR letters 'LI'; the page prints none. The baby Moses was found among bulrushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Film rushes are the first unedited prints of a day's shooting, and Moses was found as an infant in a basket among bulrushes.

clue.text: Tease the crank for not being hearty

indicators.note: to crank is to turn a handle, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Mock the eccentric because he is not a sporty type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crank' rearranges TEASETHE. At old-fashioned Oxford, 'hearties' were sporty types and the arty set were their opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: In university slang the arty, art-loving type was set against the hearty, sporting one.

clue.text: Headed police off

parts.note: headed in the sense of ran a firm, was in charge
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Someone led the police away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of the action but is the definition, as in food gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off smells stale and spoiled, which is what rancid describes.

clue.text: The home of animal husbandry

parts.note: husbandry here jokes on husbands and wives: the biblical vessel housed beasts two by two, each male with his mate

explanation.surface: A farm college described as the centre of livestock rearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical boat carried every animal in pairs, so its creatures lived as married couples.

clue.text: Pronounced bonny in her youth?

annotationWithheld.why: Pronounced bonny in her youth? (8): bonny said aloud is Bonnie (Parker), a 'girl hood'; the phrase heard and the entry spelt are the same letters, so the homophone has no second spelling the grammar accepts and a cd is refused as a downgrade

clue.text: Little Corporal, they say, cut the knave

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a surgeon does a boil
the jack is the knave in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Napoleon, the 'Little Corporal', is said to have stabbed a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Corporal' wants to be Napoleon's nickname; it is the junior army rank, and 'they say' marks the soldiers' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Lance-jack is British army slang for a lance corporal, the lowest grade of corporal.

clue.text: Not exactly a top-liner in the world's crime busters

indicators.note: not exactly says the letters are not exactly as given and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A headline act is not quite counted among the world's police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly' rearranges TOPLINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation coordinating forces across the globe.

clue.text: Suffering, from sting, and distressed

indicators.note: distressed suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is in pain from a sting and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges STING and AND together; 'Suffering' is the putting-up-with sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer something in the old sense is to tolerate it, as in 'I can't stand it'.

clue.text: A painstaking pleasure-seeker?

parts.note: painstaking is read literally as taking pain, so this is someone who finds enjoyment in cruelty

explanation.definitionFit: A person who gets pleasure from inflicting suffering on others.

clue.text: Can the minister include a song of praise?

indicators.note: include says the letters lie within the run of words can the minister

explanation.surface: A churchgoer asks whether the vicar can add a hymn to the service.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'cAN THE Minister'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or choral work of praise or loyalty is called an anthem.

clue.text: A line spoken in the script is defamatory

indicators.note: in says the spoken phrase goes inside the abbreviation for the script

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a written script

indicators.note: spoken means we hear the words a line said aloud and write what we hear

parts.note: the phrase a line, said aloud, sounds like align

explanation.surface: A line of dialogue in the screenplay is libellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns the two words 'A line' into the verb meaning to put in a row, and 'in' sets that inside the script's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them falsely, which is what a slanderous remark does.

clue.text: Diplomatic individual for a spokesman

indicators.note: for a spokesman means as a speaker would say it, so we want a word that sounds alike

parts.note: discrete means separate, individual

explanation.surface: A tactful person to act as spokesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discreet means being tactful and careful in what you say, like a good diplomat.

clue.text: Sort of furniture the salesman starts to rave over

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of rave is used

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A salesman starts to enthuse about a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro furniture is reproduction, made in the style of older antiques.

clue.text: Happened to act the part of the unlovable doctor

parts.note: to be Hamlet is to act the part of Hamlet
Dr Fell of the rhyme 'I do not love thee, Dr Fell'

explanation.surface: Something occurred while playing the role of a disliked doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The old nursery rhyme begins 'I do not love thee, Doctor Fell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is the old word for occurred or took place.

clue.text: English cricket team finds way to survive

parts.note: a cricket team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The English cricket side manages to hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live, to go on being.

clue.text: Clothing to be changed en route

explanation.surface: Clothes to be swapped on the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, and a car's gears are shifted while driving along.

clue.text: Old bag writing endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for writing loses its last letter

parts.note: script means handwriting or writing

explanation.surface: An unpleasant old woman keeps on writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bag' wants to be an insult; it is a scrip, a pilgrim's satchel of old.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrip was a small satchel or wallet carried by travellers in former times.

clue.text: Getting ready before shaving

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a paring is a thin shaving cut off

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready for the day before a shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing is making things ready in advance.

clue.text: Society girl having a perm is quick on her feet

parts.note: rollers are curlers used to give hair a perm or set
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A society woman in curlers is light on her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick on her feet' is a playful definition: wearing these she moves fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots with wheels on make the wearer move fast, so they are what is quick on her feet.
